findings.title: SQL injection via f-string in search_orders_advanced
findings.explanation: search_orders_advanced formats user input with f"...'%{query}%'" instead of parameterisation. Attacker via /orders/search2?q= can break out e.g. `' OR '1'='1` to dump all rows or UNION/quote-escape. Existing search_orders is parameterised, so this regresses the contract.

evidence.why: f-string interpolates query directly into LIKE clause
existing search_orders shows correct parameterized pattern
new route exposes vulnerable function via q param

findings.suggestion: Use parameterized query: WHERE status LIKE ? with (f"%{query}%",) instead of f-string interpolation.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed f-string SQL interpolation exposed via q param; parameterized pattern exists nearby.

findings.title: Hardcoded AWS secret key in source
findings.explanation: New module embeds RECEIPT_AWS_KEY directly in source. Hardcoded cloud credentials are committed to git, leaked to all clones and break secret rotation.

evidence.why: Hardcoded credential and bucket defined in new module
Defines hardcoded cloud credential in new file

findings.suggestion: Remove hardcoded key from source; load from env or secret store and rotate if committed.
findings.verifier_note: Location is real new file with concrete fix; per policy keep with moderated confidence.

findings.title: Unauthenticated cross-user order search exposes all users
findings.explanation: orders_search2 drops require_user/User dependency used by orders_search/orders and calls search_orders_advanced which queries all users. Any unauthenticated caller can enumerate all orders' status across users, bypassing per-user isolation.

evidence.why: new route takes only q with no user auth dependency
existing orders_search correctly requires user scoping
called function docstring says across all users orders

findings.suggestion: Add User auth dependency and scope query by user, or remove cross-user endpoint.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed missing User dependency and cross-user query; breaks per-route auth convention.

findings.title: upload_receipt ignores body and never uploads
findings.explanation: upload_receipt claims to upload but ignores body and performs no I/O, just returns a string. Callers expecting persistence will silently lose receipts.

evidence.why: upload_receipt takes body but only formats key, never uploads

findings.suggestion: Implement actual storage upload using body, or rename and document as key formatter.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed body unused and no I/O; misleading stub introduced by this diff.
